findspot: Temple of Amun M.260, steps of Room M.275, Meroe
notes: Transcription_raw follows Hallof 2024 Vol. 7, 58 as printed in Elfiky 2025, 407-408. Two earlier readings differ. Griffith (Garstang et al. 1911, 70-71, pl. LXVIII, 13) reads the signs in left-to-right order: ilro sey:olmhrbw / iyekn:ilekedisniy / ileked isniy:ilekodekm / oremn. Heyler (1966-1967, 132 n.91) reads: w-br h-mle-y sere-i yi-nsi-deke-li: nke-yi Mke-deke-li: yi-nsi-deke-li: nhe-re. Hallof notes the -ye ending was added by the scribe after the word divider was cut in the wrong place, so -ye is a formative suffix for personal names. Nmlro is unknown from other texts. The graffito on the same block may date to the mid-1st century BCE, older than the inscription. The right fragment (EC 1304) bears graffito only and no text. Date follows Rilly and Hallof (3rd century CE, Meroitic Tardif). Certainty_words lists ye by form match only: the lexicon's certain glosses for ye are south/southern region and optative/3rd-person verbal prefix, neither of which is the personal-name suffix use here.

translation:
(1) wbrḫmlo (Personal Name), Oh Osiris!
(2) It's satisfying the notable revered (Designation of wbrḫmlo), Nkeyi (Personal name).
(3) Oh Makedoke! It's satisfying the notable revered (Designation of Nkeyi).
(4) Nmlro unknown from other texts.
